title: cross-format-sampling-preserver-and-retention-mapper
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem:
Several of our downstream tracing sinks (Tempo for long-term storage, and legacy Jaeger collectors for a subset of customers) interpret sampling metadata differently. When we receive traces from heterogeneous SDKs and relay them through the platform, sampling decisions and 'sampled' flags can be lost or transformed during format translation (e.g., OTLP -> Jaeger Thrift, or OTLP/GRPC -> Tempo ingestion envelope). This causes two operational issues: 1) downstream retention/ingestion policies misclassify traces and either drop important low-volume traces or retain excessive noisy traces; 2) our sampling-aware dashboards and SLO regressions become noisy and not comparable across regions and customers.

Goal:
Build a lightweight compatibility adapter that preserves sampling intent across format boundaries and maps sampling metadata into a canonical retention hint that Tempo and legacy collectors can consume. The adapter should: 1) attach a canonical sampling hint header/attribute on outgoing envelopes; 2) translate vendor-specific sampling tags into the canonical hint; 3) expose controls for conservatively elevating retention for traces that match certain high-value criteria (error=true, duration>Xms, user-identified-transaction=true).

Approach:
1) Input normalization: Inspect incoming OpenTelemetry (OTel) envelopes and legacy Jaeger payloads to extract sampling markers (traceflags, jaeger.sampled tag, custom attributes). Normalize into an internal "sampling_intent" field (values: "keep_high", "probabilistic", "drop_by_default"). 2) Retention mapping: Implement a retention-mapper module that emits either Tempo-compatible labels (tempo_keep: true/false) and/or a lightweight downstream header for legacy collectors (X-Redwood-Retention: keep_high|probabilistic|drop). 3) Backwards compatibility: For legacy Jaeger endpoints that only accept Thrift/UDP, embed a jaeger.mapped_sampling tag where possible and dual-write a small JSON metadata envelope over HTTP as a sidecar for retention hints. 4) Config & rollout: Console feature flags to enable/disable per-tenant and per-region mapping; default to opt-in for customers on legacy integrations.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Adding metadata increases envelope size and a small amount of CPU on conversion paths; we will gate on throughput tests to keep latency < 5ms p50 on hot paths.
- Dual-write to legacy collectors is a compatibility hack; maintainers should treat it as temporary while customers migrate.
- Conservative defaults will bias towards keeping traces to avoid data loss for debug scenarios; we will provide controls to limit increased storage cost.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end test suite demonstrating preservation of sample intent for three representative SDK inputs (OTel-Go sampled, OTel-JS sampled=false, Jaeger SDK with custom sampling tag).
- Integration test asserting Tempo ingestion receives tempo_keep:true for heuristics-matched traces and that legacy Jaeger collector receives jaeger.mapped_sampling tag when mapping enabled.
- Performance benchmark: no more than 10% CPU overhead on the conversion worker and <5ms added latency p50 for conversion path under synthetic load matching 95th percentile traffic patterns.
- Console controls added: per-tenant toggle and documentation page in Confluence with migration notes.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: unit tests + local integration harness (mock Tempo + mock Jaeger).
- Week 2: canary rollout to dedicated infra (internal dev tenants) with retention logging and billing delta monitoring.
- Week 3: customer opt-in program for legacy Jaeger tenants and full release behind feature flag.

Metrics and monitoring:
- New metrics: sampling_mapping_rate, sampling_mapping_errors, retention_hint_emit_rate, retention_hook_latency_ms p50/p95.
- Dashboards: add a retention-mapper panel to tracing health dashboard showing mapped vs original sampling distribution by tenant and region.
- Alerts: sampling_mapping_errors > 0.1% over 5m -> P1 pager.

Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.company.com/display/OBS/Cross-Format+Sampling+Preserver (internal)
- Integration harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-harness/pulls/128
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-relay/pull/402

Notes:
- Coordinate with Platform Security early if any headers or sidecar metadata cross untrusted network boundaries.
- Reach out to Solutions Eng for a list of legacy Jaeger customers who must be migrated before turning on default mapping.
